title: Little Signs
summary: Sign<Tech> is piloting Little Signs, a speech-to-sign-language tool, at a Zimbabwean school; no source reports a measured result in the classroom.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Little Signs was founded on 26 March 2024, according to an entry by its team in the TotalEnergies Startupper challenge. The entry describes it as a Zimbabwe Sign Language learning app for preschoolers and states that it was not yet selling. In June 2025 the team's account in an International Telecommunication Union report described a pilot of speech-to-sign-language support at King George the 4th Secondary School in Zimbabwe. The account reports no measured gain in access or participation in the classroom. In February 2026 the Little Signs website offered animated Zimbabwe Sign Language lessons for children and reported no results from the school pilot.
purpose: Make spoken classroom content accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing learners.
deployer: King George the 4th Secondary School pilot

ratings.reason: The pilot is intended to improve communication and participation in class for deaf and hard-of-hearing learners; no impact result is reported.
Schools are intended to provide more accessible instruction; the extent of improvement is unmeasured.
